newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks rattled by earnings warnings.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks rattled by earnings warnings.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks fell Wednesday as earnings warnings from high-technology companies cast a shadow over Wall Street, encouraging investors to cash profits from the market's recent strong gains.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 47.05 points at 7,713.73.
In the broader market, declining issues beat advances 13-9 on moderate volume of 278 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index, which is laced with high-tech stocks, was off 11.60 points at 1,431.51.
"It probably is a little profit-taking after the run-up," said Alfred Kugel, senior investment strategist for Stein Roe.
He said the fallout from the technology warnings was confined to specific stocks.
Gateway 2000 Inc., which said late Tuesday that its second-quarter revenues would be about even with the first quarter, saw its stock lose 2-3/8 at 32-3/8.
Seagate Technology Inc. tumbled 5-1/4 to 36-1/8 after saying that its quarterly revenues would be below its earlier forecast.
But analysts said the market remains strong despite the day's drop because investors are buying on the dips.

"It's very interesting that whenever we see any kind of a selloff in this market ... The market has an initial selloff and then tends to rebound," said Sam Stovall, director of industry information at S&P Industry Surveys.
"People are discounting the bad news and that is the difference between a bull market and a bear market," he said.
Pierre Ellis, senior economist at Primark Decision Economics, said another factor that might be affecting the market was the strong upward revision of the first-quarter non-farm productivity.
The Labour Department said the revised first-quarter gain of 2.6 percent in non-farm productivity, up from 2.0 percent previously, was the largest since the fourth quarter of 1993.

Ellis said this figure, coupled with strong data on industrial production Tuesday, suggested an "undertone" of inflationary currents that may sway the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, not at their July meeting but perhaps at the next one.
Wall Street punished Oracle Corp. after the software company failed to match optimistic forecasts for its quarterly results. The shares slid 2-3/4 to 50-1/2.
Intel Corp., a bellwether technology stock, was off 2-11/16 to 147 and Microsoft Corp. fell 3-3/16 to 131.
